summary: Hardened the graceful self-restart (apphost.Restarter, used by the UI restart button, backup restore, factory reset and self-update) so it can never spawn an unbounded storm of processes/console windows on Windows. Three fixes, all OS-aware: (1) the Windows self-relaunch now creates the detached child with CREATE_NO_WINDOW instead of DETACHED_PROCESS — DETACHED_PROCESS made Windows allocate a brand-new console window for the console-subsystem binary on every relaunch (the stray 'DOS command' windows), so a relaunch loop spammed windows until the machine had to be rebooted; (2) a cross-OS self-relaunch storm guard bounds relaunches to 5 within 60s (counted across the relaunch chain via KOPIV2_RESTART_GEN/KOPIV2_RESTART_T0 env, which the child inherits) and then stays DOWN with a clear log rather than looping, so a crash-on-boot or any immediate re-restart halts instead of running away; a window that elapses resets the count so ordinary restarts are never throttled; (3) a process running as a Windows service is now detected (svc.IsWindowsService) and treated as supervised, so it exits with restartExitCode for the SCM to relaunch instead of self-spawning a detached child that escapes the service and races a fresh service instance for the listen port.
compatibility: No API or config changes. Behavior change: a Windows *service* run now exits for the SCM on restart (as systemd/Docker/KOPIV2_SUPERVISED already did) rather than self-relaunching — service installs should configure failure-recovery (sc failure / WinSW <onfailure>) or set KOPIV2_SUPERVISED=1 so the manager restarts it; a bare/interactive Windows run still self-relaunches, now without a console window. Unix behavior is unchanged (execve in place). The storm guard only trips on >5 relaunches inside 60s, which normal use never reaches.
